paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when the whole crowd is panicking, you don't have to join them. The LORD told Isaiah, "Do not fear what they fear; do not live in dread." (Isaiah 8:12) Only the LORD of Hosts is the One to fear, and He is also the One who will be a sanctuary (Isaiah 8:13-14). So the baker's job is to wait on Him and hold tight to His word, because the other voices, mediums included, only leave people roaming in the dark (Isaiah 8:17, 19-22).

And then comes my favorite word in the whole passage: NEVERTHELESS. (Isaiah 9:1) The people walking in darkness did not find their own way out, and neither can we. The light came to them: "The people walking in darkness have seen a great light." (Isaiah 9:2) Friend, I spent years in a dark drawer, so I can tell you, a light you didn't earn is the best kind of light.

The light has a name, and it's a child. "For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, and the government will be upon His shoulders." (Isaiah 9:6) He is Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father and Prince of Peace, and His peace has no end (Isaiah 9:6-7). Who makes it happen? "The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this." (Isaiah 9:7) So, baker, you can rest your heart, because the work is His and not yours, and that is why my ovens stay ready.
